prompt: Create an original editorial illustration for the About opening of Code Like It's 198x, a website about understanding computers deeply and using that understanding to make games. Wide full-bleed panoramic composition, approximately 3:1. This must feel more substantial and intellectually curious than a child's making kit, and different from a paper debugging workbench. On the right half, show an imagined compact vintage computer opened into an elegant sculptural cutaway: a cream outer casing lifted above an anonymous keyboard, a floating dark green circuit plane beneath, and a few thin translucent amber layers between them. Around and just above the opening, small square coloured paper pixels gather into a simple abstract picture, as though revealing how a visible result is built from physical layers. The relationship is poetic and deliberately illustrative, not a labelled technical diagram or an accurate service-manual exploded view. Give each material a convincing physical presence and deep soft cast shadows. A few components and paper pixel fragments can cross the imagined image margin and extend beyond the outer frame. Reserve the left forty percent as quiet warm cream paper for later live typography, with a very restrained faint transition into the physical scene. Charcoal, warm ivory, deep green circuitry, amber and selective vermilion/cobalt pixel pieces; strong form rather than many tiny details. Premium dimensional editorial art, warm raking studio light, subtly printed paper texture, inviting curiosity rather than cyberpunk spectacle. No magnifier, graph paper pile, literal arrows or network, portraits, readable text, code, labels, logos or recognisable commercial machine design. No actual software screen or purported historical artefact. The machine and its layers are imagined original illustration. No border or UI boxes. No title in the raster.
